items.title: Frank Chace Interview, 1961-11-18
items.q: Al Jenkins is a great player. He's now in Los Angeles. I don't know. I hope he's doing all right. A great trombone player.

ctx.x: Were there other clarinet players with the Bobcats who might have left an influence here, Detroit, or anywhere?

Oh, sure. Nappy Trottier, who does he like? Beric? Well, Berrigan didn't play with the Bobcats. Let's see. Butterfield is almost universally, it seems to me, admired by trumpet players. And I know Butterfield put in a tour of duty with the Bobcats. Al Jenkins is a great player. He's now in Los Angeles. I don't know. I hope he's doing all right. A great trombone player. And he loved the Bobcats, but it's hard to think exactly which trombone player he... Teagarden was his man. But the Warren Smith with the Bobcats,…

Well, you've deviated a little. I wondered if there were other clarinets than Fozola who might have left a stamp. Was Eddie Miller playing enough clarinet with the Bobcats that anybody speaks about him today? He says, this is an Eddie Miller soul?
